newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HOOGOVENS IN STEEL PAY DEAL WITH UNIONS.
newsitem.headline: HOOGOVENS IN STEEL PAY DEAL WITH UNIONS.

text.p: Hoogovens NV said on Thursday it had struck a deal on pay and working conditions with labour unions, thus averting the threat of a strike at its main IJmuiden steel works.
Hoogovens said the agreement also set out terms for a phased reduction in the number of steel workers in IJmuiden from 10,500 to 8,500 by the year 2002.
The agreement still has to be approved by union members, but union leaders have said they will recommend its approval.
Under the two-year deal employees will receive two pay rises of 2.75 percent on April 1, 1997 and on April 1, 1998.
Hoogovens has also pledged that nobody will be forced out of their job despite the reduction in the work force which the company says is needed to raise productivity and stay competitive.
Instead Hoogovens will extend early retirement and part-time working schemes for older employees.
The labour agreement does not apply to employees of the group's aluminium business.
